entries.summary: wsMUSD seeded with 1 MUSD of dead shares, deposited into the real sMUSD.
entries.proves: The ERC-4626 wrapper composes with Mezo's live claim-based sMUSD and is protected against first-depositor inflation.

entries.summary: BorrowAccountFactory deployed; its constructor deploys the bcBTC receipt and the BorrowAccount implementation.
entries.proves: The account factory, gated collateral receipt and clone implementation fit in one transaction under Mezo's 10M block gas limit.

entries.summary: M1 created on Mezo's official testnet Morpho Blue: MUSD loan, bcBTC collateral, BtcMusdOracle, AdaptiveCurveIrm, LLTV 0.77.
entries.proves: A redemption-free BTC→MUSD market now exists on Mezo's own Morpho deployment, created permissionlessly.

entries.summary: Team supplied 3,000 MUSD of liquidity to M1.
entries.proves: Judges can borrow immediately; vMUSD now tops this liquidity up through its allocator.

entries.summary: openAndBorrow: 0.001 BTC sent as msg.value, 30 MUSD borrowed in one transaction (0.1% origination fee).
entries.proves: One-transaction BTC→MUSD credit priced by the live Skip precompile, with no 2,000-MUSD minimum and no redemption queue.

entries.summary: repayAndWithdraw: debt repaid exactly by shares, collateral withdrawn and unwrapped to native BTC in one transaction.
entries.proves: The oracle-free exit path works on-chain; debt and collateral are both zero afterwards.

entries.summary: Judge journey (e2e harness, real signing wallet): claimed 25 test MUSD from the dispenser in the Get test funds card.
entries.proves: The faucet top-up a judge needs for interest and the fee works from the UI.

entries.summary: Judge journey: one MUSD permit signature, then depositWithPermit put 5 MUSD into wsMUSD (5 shares) in one transaction.
entries.proves: The Save flow needs no separate approval for EOAs: permit and deposit land together on Mezo testnet.

entries.summary: Judge journey: redeemInKind burned the remaining 3 wsMUSD for 3 sMUSD sent straight to the wallet.
entries.proves: wsMUSD’s exit that bypasses sMUSD deposits and withdrawals works on the live sMUSD.

entries.summary: Judge journey: one permit, then repayAndWithdrawWithPermit repaid 21.76 MUSD and returned 0.0009 native BTC.
entries.proves: The oracle-free, one-transaction exit works from the UI with a MUSD permit, to the wei.

entries.summary: vMUSD created through Mezo’s own VaultV2Factory (Morpho Vault V2, MUSD asset).
entries.proves: The lending vault is a standard Morpho Vault V2 instance that Mezo’s factory recognises.

entries.summary: WsMusdLiquidityAdapter deployed: vMUSD’s liquidity adapter that parks idle MUSD in wsMUSD.
entries.proves: Deposits earn sMUSD yield until borrowers need the MUSD, and a full wsMUSD cannot block deposits.

entries.summary: BaserateAllocator deployed: no owner, a 2,000 MUSD / 15% M1 buffer, at most 1,000 MUSD per move, 1-hour cooldown.
entries.proves: Allocation follows a fixed public policy anyone can trigger, inside the curator’s caps.

entries.summary: vMUSD seeded with 100 MUSD of dead shares, allocated straight into wsMUSD by the liquidity adapter.
entries.proves: The vault is inflation-protected and the deposit → wsMUSD path works on the live contracts.

entries.summary: Deployer’s temporary allocator role removed; adapter, cap, allocator and fee changes put behind a 48-hour timelock.
entries.proves: Only BaserateAllocator can move vMUSD funds; adapter and cap changes are visible two days ahead.

entries.summary: 3,000 MUSD deposited into vMUSD (3,000 vMUSD minted); the liquidity adapter moved it into wsMUSD in the same call.
entries.proves: Lenders get vMUSD 1:1 and their MUSD earns sMUSD yield from the first block.

entries.summary: First permissionless rebalance: BUFFER_TOP_UP moved 1,000 MUSD from wsMUSD into M1 (M1 liquidity was 876 vs a 2,000 target).
entries.proves: The allocator keeps borrowers’ M1 buffer filled from the vault without any privileged key.

entries.summary: Backstop (bMUSD) deployed: an ERC-4626 over MUSD that buys seized BTC at the oracle price less half the 7.41% incentive.
entries.proves: Liquidations have a buyer of last resort on testnet that does not depend on DEX depth.

entries.summary: FlashLiquidator deployed, bound to M1 and the backstop, with the vAMM venue and a 6.89% maximum price impact.
entries.proves: Anyone can liquidate M1 with zero capital: the seized BTC is sold inside Morpho’s callback.

entries.summary: Backstop seeded with 1 MUSD of dead shares, parked in wsMUSD.
entries.proves: The backstop is live, protected against first-depositor inflation, and earns sMUSD yield on idle cash.

entries.summary: openCanary: 0.002 BTC posted and 123.47 MUSD borrowed at ≈76.7% LTV against the 77% LLTV (CANARY profile).
entries.proves: A live position sits one small BTC dip from liquidation, so the liquidation path can be exercised on real state.

entries.summary: FeeRouter deployed: an ownerless 40/40/20 splitter to sMUSD yield, the testnet BTC/MUSD gauge’s bribe and the treasury.
entries.proves: The bribe target was checked against PoolsVoter.gaugeToBribe at construction; the split cannot be changed.

entries.summary: Governor submitted setFeeRecipient(FeeRouter) on the factory; executable after the 48-hour timelock (27 Oct 19:02 UTC).
entries.proves: Fee changes go through the factory’s public timelock: anyone can see them coming two days ahead.

entries.summary: distribute(): 20 MUSD split into an 8 MUSD bribe on the BTC/MUSD gauge for epoch 1792627200, 8 MUSD to sMUSD, 4 to treasury.
entries.proves: Fees reach veBTC voters (claimable after the Thursday flip) and sMUSD holders through Mezo’s own contracts.

entries.summary: RiskLens deployed: one eth_call returns oracle, market, caps, backstop, depth quotes and the trove queue.
entries.proves: The Risk page reads everything from one stateless contract within Mezo’s precompile limit.
